- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially when sentiment is >0.5 and recent prices are rising.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or corrections when sentiment is negative or near-zero.
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes; reduce forecast magnitude by 5–15% if sentiment is low or neutral after a spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 10–20% if sentiment is weak or negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates early in the period; adjust downward by 3–8% if sentiment is declining or sentiment history shows divergence.
- When sentiment is consistently positive but prices are falling, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in trend continuation.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is above recent 10-day average, apply a downward correction of 10–15% to avoid overcompensation.
